app.name: Plinto
app.description: Everything your family spends, in one calm place.

demoBanner.text: You're in the example household. This data is invented.

subtitle.debts: What the household owes in total
subtitle.obligations: What the household owes this month

accounts.description: This is where your money lives: bank, cash, savings, or a digital wallet. Loans you pay in installments are an account too, of type debt.
accounts.title: Accounts

categories.description: Optional, and they show you where your money goes. Use them if you want your expenses organized by type.
categories.title: Categories

credit.description: Cards and revolving credit aren't accounts: they have a limit. Each statement you record becomes an obligation with its own due date.
credit.title: Credit

debts.description: These are purchases financed in fixed installments. Each month, Plinto generates one obligation for the installment due.
debts.title: Debts

firstSteps.description: This checklist walks you through your household's first tasks. Work through it at your own pace from here.
firstSteps.title: First steps

help.description: You can replay this tour anytime from here. Settings holds members, export, and language.
help.title: Need help?

household.description: A household is shared: whoever manages it is the owner, whoever logs entries is a member, and whoever only looks is a viewer. You can belong to more than one household and switch between them here.
household.title: Your household

obligations.description: This is what you owe this month. Its status — pending, paid, or overdue — is only ever calculated from the payments you reconcile; you never set it by hand.
obligations.title: Obligations

transactions.description: Every income or expense you log comes out of an account. Transfers move money between your accounts (not expenses), and recurring ones repeat monthly until they become obligations.
transactions.title: Transactions

welcome.description: This tour shows you how to use Plinto and the ideas behind its data. It takes a minute and saves you confusion later.
welcome.title: Plinto tells you what you owe, what you have, and what's coming

authLayout.pitch: Track accounts, transactions and categories across every household you manage — in one place.

empty.description: An obligation is something you must pay this month: rent, utilities, instalments, cards. Plinto tells you what is pending, what you paid and what is overdue. Its status comes from the payments you link, not something you mark by hand.

empty.description: This is for your cards and revolving credit lines. They are not accounts: they have a limit, and every statement you record becomes an obligation with its own due date.

form.creatingNote: No cutoff or payment day here. Each statement brings its own dates, so a lender switching you from monthly to biweekly needs nothing changed.
form.currencyFixedHint: Fixed — the statements below carry their own amounts

statementForm.editingNote: The payment on the obligations board changes with it. It cannot go below what you have already paid against this statement — undo the payment first if the issuer really lowered it after you paid.
statementForm.overLimit: That is {amount} over your limit — recorded as it is, not refused.
statementForm.statementDateFixedHint: Fixed — it decides which month this belongs to

validation.ACCOUNTS_MUST_DIFFER: Source and destination accounts must differ
validation.AT_LEAST_ONE_FIELD: At least one field must be provided
validation.DUE_DATE_INSIDE_PERIOD: The due date must fall inside the period
validation.DUE_WITHIN_BALANCE: The amount due cannot exceed the closing balance
validation.LAST_INSTALLMENT_EMPTY: The installments already cover the whole principal; the last one would be empty
validation.invalidEnumValue: Pick one of the available options
validation.invalidString: That value is not in a valid format

apiErrors.ALREADY_A_MEMBER: That person is already a member of this household.
apiErrors.CATEGORY_TYPE_MISMATCH: That category does not apply to this kind of transaction.
apiErrors.CREDIT_LINE_CLOSED: That credit line is closed and no longer accepts statements.
apiErrors.CREDIT_LINE_NOT_FOUND: That credit line no longer exists.
apiErrors.CREDIT_STATEMENT_BELOW_PAID: The amount cannot go below what has already been paid against this statement.
apiErrors.CREDIT_STATEMENT_DUE_ABOVE_BALANCE: The amount due cannot exceed the closing balance.
apiErrors.CREDIT_STATEMENT_DUE_BEFORE_CUTOFF: The payment date cannot fall before the statement date.
apiErrors.DEBT_ACCOUNT_NOT_A_LIABILITY: That account is not a liability, so it cannot carry a debt.
apiErrors.DEMO_TENANT_EXISTS: You already have an example household. You can go to it or delete it from Settings.
apiErrors.INVITATION_EMAIL_REQUIRED: An email address is required to send the invitation.
apiErrors.LAST_OWNER: A household must keep at least one owner.
apiErrors.LENDER_NOT_A_LIABILITY: The lender account must be a liability.
apiErrors.LOAN_CURRENCY_MISMATCH: Both accounts must use the same currency.
apiErrors.LOAN_DESTINATION_IS_A_LIABILITY: The destination account cannot be a liability.
apiErrors.OBLIGATION_CURRENCY_MISMATCH: The payment currency does not match the obligation.
apiErrors.RECURRING_RULE_NOT_FOUND: That recurring rule no longer exists.
apiErrors.REPORT_INVALID_PERIOD: That reporting period is not valid.
apiErrors.REQUEST_FAILED: The request could not be completed. Please try again.
apiErrors.TENANT_NOT_DEMO: This household isn't the example one, so it can't be deleted here.
apiErrors.TRANSACTION_NOT_AN_EXPENSE: Only an expense can be applied here.
apiErrors.TRANSFER_FX_NOT_ALLOWED: A transfer between accounts in the same currency cannot carry an exchange rate.
apiErrors.TRANSFER_FX_REQUIRED: A transfer between different currencies needs an exchange rate.
apiErrors.TRANSFER_SAME_ACCOUNT: A transfer needs two different accounts.
apiErrors.UNAUTHORIZED: Your session ended. Please sign in again.
apiErrors.UNKNOWN: Something went wrong. Please try again.
apiErrors.VALIDATION_ERROR: Some of the details are not valid. Check the fields and try again.
